description: Normalize a tracker state for comparison with Lowercase Normalization (Section 4.2; decision 0105): the Unicode Default Case Conversion to lowercase, full mappings rather than simple ones, no language-specific tailoring, and no Unicode normalization form applied. State comparisons (active/terminal membership, per-state concurrency keys, transition (from, on) uniqueness) are performed on the normalized value, which is a comparison key and not a display string. Non-ASCII code points are written as \u escapes so the property under test survives an authoring tool that would silently re-normalize a literal.

vectors.description: Fails under a Turkish tailoring, where U+0049 lowercases to U+0131 - but only on a host whose locale is Turkish, which is why the non-ASCII vectors below separate the readings on any host.

The Turkish state name 'Inceleme' whose first letter is U+0130, Latin capital I with dot above. Its full lowercase mapping is two code points, U+0069 U+0307. An ASCII-only implementation leaves U+0130 unchanged and a Turkish-tailored one yields U+0069 alone, so this vector separates all three readings irrespective of the host's locale.
U+1E9E, capital sharp s, lowercases to U+00DF. An ASCII-only implementation leaves it unchanged; a case-folding implementation yields U+0073 U+0073 ('ss'). The rule is lowercasing, not folding.

The state name 'Under Review' whose first letter is decomposed, U+0055 U+0308. No Unicode normalization form is applied, so the combining mark survives and the result starts U+0075 U+0308 rather than the precomposed U+00FC; a state spelled this way does not compare equal to the same name spelled precomposed.
